title: 1997 AMC 8 Problem 16
statement: Penni Precisely buys \(\$ 100\) worth of stock in each of three companies: Alabama Almonds, Boston Beans, and California Cauliflower. After one year, AA was up \(20 \%,\) BB was down \(25 \%,\) and CC was unchanged. For the second year, AA was down \(20 \%\) from the previous year, BB was up \(25 \%\) from the previous year, and CC was unchanged. If \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are the final values of the stock, then

solutions.text:
After the first year, AA’s stock’s worth goes up to \[ \$ 100 \cdot 1.2 = \$ 120 \] and BB’s goes down to \[ \$ 100 \cdot 0.75 = \$ 75. \]

After the second year, AA’s stock is worth \[ \$ 120 \cdot 0.8 = \$ 96 \] and BB’s is worth \[ \$ 75 \cdot 1.25 = \$ 93.75. \]

CC’s stock worth remains the same, so the ordering of the stock worths is now \[ B \lt A \lt C. \]

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: A \(20\) percent gain followed by a \(20\) percent loss does not return to the start
